sections.h2: Which office files a Darke County deed?
sections.html:
The Darke County Recorder files it. The office sits in the Greenville courthouse at 504 S. Broadway, answers at 937-547-7390, and posts weekday hours from 8 to 4.

ORC Chapter 317 governs the office, which the county describes as its official keeper of records. Besides deeds and mortgages, the recorder takes mechanic liens, powers of attorney, recognizance bonds, IRS liens, corporate franchise liens and partnership papers. The job is to record what you bring, so a deed written by you or your attorney needs to be finished before it arrives.

sections.h2: What must be done to a deed before the recorder accepts it?
sections.html:
A deed needs the grantor's signature, an acknowledgment, and the auditor's stamp before it goes to the recorder. Under ORC 5301.01, the grantor acknowledges the signing before a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor, and that official certifies the acknowledgment.

In Darke County the usual order runs like this:

  1. Draft the deed with a legal description that matches the parcel. The county engineer keeps the tax maps and reviews deeds, land transfers and lot splits for proper boundary descriptions.
  2. Sign and acknowledge the deed.
  3. Take the deed and a conveyance fee statement to the Darke County Auditor on the courthouse first floor. The auditor's forms page lists DTE 100 for a standard conveyance, DTE 100EX for an exempt one, DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for farmland valued at its agricultural use.
  4. Pay the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax to the auditor, get the stamp, and bring the deed to the recorder.

Bring these to the auditor's counter:

  • The signed and acknowledged deed with its legal description.
  • A completed conveyance fee statement on the right DTE form.
  • Payment for the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax.

Splitting a lot off a larger parcel adds a step. The county's own contact list sends split questions to the zoning inspector at 937-547-7381, and building permits for the unincorporated areas, the city of Greenville and a list of villages run through the county building regulation office at 937-547-7379.

sections.h2: What are the Darke County recording charges?
sections.html:
The schedule comes from ORC 317.32. A standard deed or mortgage pays $17 plus a matching $17 housing trust fund fee through page two, then $4 plus $4 for every further page. Counties may add a preservation surcharge of as much as $5 a document. Ask the recorder whether Darke County collects it, and how much.

StepOfficeWhat you leave with
Boundary checkCounty engineerSign-off on the legal description
Value statement and feesCounty auditorStamped deed
FilingCounty recorderRecorded instrument

The same statute prices copies. A certified copy costs a $1 base fee and a $1 housing trust fund fee per page, a recorder's seal on the certification adds $0.50 and $0.50, and a marginal reference entered through a separate instrument costs $2 and $2. Charges fall due when the paper is presented, and each page, caption page included, counts at its 8.5 by 14 inch size or fraction of one (ORC 317.32).

sections.h2: Which side of a Darke County sale pays the transfer costs?
sections.html:
The seller. ORC 319.202(D) assigns the grantor the conveyance fee under section 319.54(G)(3), and also any transfer tax the commissioners adopted under Chapter 322. A county transfer tax may not exceed thirty cents per hundred dollars of value and is paid to the auditor before recording (ORC 322.02). Ask the Darke County auditor if one is in place.

For a sale, value means the full price paid or to be paid, mortgage or vendor's lien included. For a gift it means the likely open-market price, and willful falsification is prohibited. The auditor's site offers a calculator that takes a parcel count and sale price and includes the parcel transfer fee, so test the figure before closing.

sections.h2: What does the Darke County auditor check on a deed?
sections.html:
The stamp is the auditor's way of telling the recorder that the paperwork is complete. ORC 319.202 has the buyer or the buyer's representative file the value statement. The auditor then marks the deed with the fee and compliance, keeps the original, and sends the tax commissioner a copy that notes the latest assessed value.

Two sets of affirmations ride on that statement. The first covers a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction on the current or prior year's tax. The second covers agricultural valuation. If the answer to either is yes, both sides sign a sworn instrument that accounts for the reduction or for the recoupment charge. For residential rental property, the indorsement also reminds the buyer of landlord information due under ORC 5323.02.

For a family transfer or other exempt deed, the statement only needs the reason for the exemption. Pick the exempt form (DTE 100EX) and state the reason plainly.

sections.h2: How far back do online Darke County land records reach?
sections.html:
The recorder's page offers an online search of land records beginning May 1996 and says the index was due to reach back to January 1980 by the end of 2023. Ask the office how far back it runs now, and how to view older books in person.

A free Property Fraud Alert subscription is also on offer. It is a notification service that warns an owner when a document is recorded against the property, and it suits anyone holding a vacant house.

  • Parcel searches, the county map and the sales report live on the auditor's website, not at the recorder.
  • Questions about value or tax on a parcel go to the auditor, and questions about what is already of record go to the recorder.

sections.h2: What history and roads frame Darke County land records?
sections.html:
Settlement began at Fort Jefferson in 1791, and the Treaty of Greenville was signed at Fort Greenville in 1795, ceding southern Ohio to the United States. Darke County was created in 1809 and organized in 1817, the first railroad reached it in 1850, and by the late twentieth century the economy mixed farming with manufacturing while many residents commuted to Dayton.

The 2020 census found 51,881 residents, a median age of 42.5, and 20.8 percent of people at least 65. It counted 20,925 households, 28.8 percent of them one-person households. Land that families have held for decades makes the legal description important, and the county engineer reviews deeds for proper boundary descriptions.

The county's villages include Ansonia, Arcanum, Castine, Gettysburg, Ithaca, New Madison, New Weston, Pitsburg, Union City, Versailles, Wayne Lakes and Yorkshire, and cities, villages and townships hold the zoning authority for their own ground. Main roads include US 127, US 36 and State Routes 49, 47, 121 and 118. Public school districts reaching into the county include Greenville City, Versailles Exempted Village, Ansonia Local, Arcanum-Butler Local, Bradford Exempted Village, Mississinawa Valley Local, Tri-Village Local and National Trail Local, among others, and a deed's parcel record shows the district for tax purposes. A house in an unzoned township answers to the township trustees on zoning, so confirm that before you list.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Darke County Recorder?
faqs.a: Call 937-547-7390 or go to the courthouse at 504 S. Broadway in Greenville. The county lists the office as open on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is the Darke County filing charge based on page count?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio sets one price for the first two pages and a lower price per added page, and a preservation surcharge of up to $5 may apply on top. ORC 317.32 has the list.

faqs.q: Which comes first in Darke County, auditor or recorder?
faqs.a: The auditor. The conveyance fee statement and fee earn the stamp, and the recorder then files the stamped deed.

faqs.q: Is a homemade deed acceptable in Darke County?
faqs.a: It can be brought in, but it needs a signature, an acknowledgment before an authorized official, a description the engineer's tax maps support and the auditor's stamp. A title company or attorney can prepare it.

faqs.q: Can older Darke County deeds be found online?
faqs.a: Online search starts with May 1996. The recorder planned to extend the index to January 1980, so ask what year it begins now.
